questions.question: In the office kitchen fridge, which spot is usually the warmest, making it the worst place to keep the shared milk?
questions.explanation: Every time a colleague opens the fridge, the door shelves get a blast of warm room air, so they swing up and down in temperature far more than the back of the fridge. The coldest, most stable spot for milk is usually at the back of a lower shelf.

questions.question: The word 'robot' was coined for a 1920 stage play and comes from a word meaning forced labour in which language?
questions.explanation: Karel Čapek used it in his play R.U.R., and credited his brother Josef with suggesting the word.

questions.question: Someone very drunk is 'three sheets to the wind'. On a sailing ship, those 'sheets' aren't sails at all. What are they?
questions.explanation: Sheets are the ropes that trim a sail. Let three of them run loose and the sails flap uselessly while the ship lurches about like a sailor after shore leave.

questions.question: A newborn Dalmatian puppy is missing the one feature the breed is famous for. What is it missing?
questions.explanation: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white, and their spots only start appearing after about two weeks. So a real litter would look nothing like the cartoon.

questions.question: Myslivci mají pro krev zvěře zvláštní slovo. Je to úplně obyčejné slovo, které byste spíš čekali u malíře. Jaké?
questions.explanation: V myslivecké mluvě se krev opravdu nazývá barva. Postřelená zvěř „barví“ a dohledává se po barvě. Podobně má zajíc místo uší slechy a liška místo ocasu oháňku.

questions.question: Samotné slovo pomlázka prozrazuje, co mělo velikonoční šlehání ženám a dívkám původně dát. Co to je?
questions.explanation: Pomlázka pochází od slova „pomladit“, tedy omladit. Mladé pružné vrbové proutky měly na šlehanou přenést svou svěžest, zdraví a mladost.

questions.question: Které české krajské město má přímo v názvu schované, že kdysi patřilo českým královnám jako jejich věno?
questions.explanation: „Králové“ znamená „královny“. Město bylo věnným městem českých královen a nejslavnější z nich, Eliška Rejčka, tam založila kostel, který stojí dodnes.

questions.question: Why does a street sound so strangely hushed right after a fresh, fluffy snowfall?
questions.explanation: Fresh snow is mostly air trapped between ice crystals, so it soaks up sound like the foam on a recording studio wall. Once it melts and refreezes into a hard crust, it reflects sound and the hush is gone.

questions.question: In Breaking Bad, chemistry teacher Walter White takes a criminal alias borrowed from a famous German physicist. That physicist is best known for a principle named after what?
questions.explanation: The alias is Heisenberg, after Werner Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. It suits a man whose true identity the police can never be sure of.

questions.question: In the 2025 Netflix animated hit KPop Demon Hunters, the girl group Huntr/x, whose song Golden topped the Billboard Hot 100, battle demons posing as a rival boy band. What is that boy band called?
questions.explanation: The name is a pun: in Korean, saja means lion, but it is also the word for the grim reapers who escort souls to the afterlife, which is precisely what the boys are.

questions.explanation: Emoji is Japanese for 'picture character', from 'e' meaning picture and 'moji' meaning character, and its similarity to 'emotion' is pure coincidence.

questions.question: Hardly any national flag uses the colour purple. What's the historical reason?
questions.explanation: For centuries purple dye came from thousands of crushed sea snails and cost more than gold, so it was reserved for royalty. Today only a handful of flags, such as Dominica's parrot, show any purple at all.

questions.question: The puzzle cube invented by architecture professor Ernő Rubik in 1974 came from which country?
questions.explanation: Rubik built it in Budapest as a teaching aid for spatial thinking and reportedly took a month to solve his own creation.

questions.question: The very first video game tournament, held at Stanford University in the early 1970s, had a modest prize: a one-year subscription to which famous music magazine?
questions.explanation: The 1972 'Intergalactic Spacewar Olympics' was organised with Rolling Stone, which covered the event. Today's top tournaments pay out millions of dollars.

questions.question: Drake landed another US top-five hit, 'Solar Eclipse', in October 2026. Before music fame, he played a basketball player who ends up in a wheelchair in which Canadian teen drama series?
questions.explanation: As Aubrey Graham, he played Jimmy Brooks in Degrassi: The Next Generation, starting in 2001. Jimmy was paralysed after being shot by a classmate.

questions.question: The word 'tsunami' is Japanese and combines two words. One means 'wave'. What does the other mean?
questions.explanation: Fishermen out at sea would notice nothing unusual, then return to find their harbour destroyed, so the word literally means 'harbour wave'.

questions.question: Na Slovensku oslavujeme Deň učiteľov 28. marca. Čie narodeniny si v tento deň vlastne pripomíname?
questions.explanation: Komenský sa narodil 28. marca 1592 a vďaka učebniciam ako Orbis pictus ho dodnes voláme učiteľom národov. Kvety pre pani učiteľku sú teda vlastne aj darček k jeho narodeninám.

questions.question: If you swap the ham in eggs Benedict for spinach, the dish takes its name from which Italian city?
questions.explanation: It becomes eggs Florentine. In classic French cooking, 'à la florentine' has long meant 'served with spinach', a nod to Florence.

questions.question: Which button-up knitted jacket is named after the British earl who led the doomed Charge of the Light Brigade?
questions.explanation: The 7th Earl of Cardigan and his officers wore knitted wool waistcoats in the Crimean War, and his fame turned his title into a wardrobe staple. The same war gave us the balaclava, named after a battle there.

questions.question: In the word 'karaoke', the Japanese 'kara' means 'empty'. The 'oke' part is a clipped borrowing of which English word?
questions.explanation: Karaoke literally means 'empty orchestra'. The band is all there on the backing track, and the only thing missing is the singer, which is you.

questions.question: Only one US state has a genuine royal palace, built for a real king and queen. Which state is it?
questions.explanation: Hawaii was an independent kingdom until 1893, and ʻIolani Palace in Honolulu was the home of its last monarchs. It even had electric lights before the White House did.

questions.question: Slovenské zvolanie „sakra“ je len skrátená podoba staršej nadávky. Z akého cirkevného pojmu vzniklo?
questions.explanation: „Sakra“ pochádza z latinského slova sacramentum, teda sviatosť. Kedysi bolo zahrešiť na niečo sväté naozaj vážne, a preto sa nadávka zjemnila na krátke „sakra“.

questions.question: Čo musí podľa známeho pokriku slovenských hokejových fanúšikov robiť každý, kto chce dokázať, že je Slovák?
questions.explanation: Pokrik znie „Kto neskáče, nie je Slovák!“, a preto pri ňom poskakujú celé tribúny aj fanzóny, od štadióna až po námestia.

questions.question: Ktoré slovenské mesto sa pre svoje bane prezýva „zlaté mesto“ a dodnes sa v ňom razia slovenské euromince?
questions.explanation: Kremnické zlaté dukáty patrili v stredoveku k najcennejším minciam v Európe. Tamojšia mincovňa razí peniaze nepretržite už takmer sedem storočí, takže euro vo vašej peňaženke pochádza z rovnakej dielne ako dukáty kráľov.

questions.question: Najväčší riečny ostrov v Európe leží na Slovensku. Obteká ho Dunaj a Malý Dunaj. Ako sa volá?
questions.explanation: Kto ide z Bratislavy do Komárna, celý čas je vlastne na ostrove, len o tom nevie. Žitný ostrov je taký veľký, že sú na ňom celé mestá vrátane Dunajskej Stredy a Veľkého Medera.

questions.question: The word 'nausea' comes from an Ancient Greek word for a means of transport. Which one?
questions.explanation: The Greek 'naus' meant ship, the same root as 'nautical', so nausea literally means seasickness. Sailors had the feeling long before anyone got carsick.

questions.question: In 2025 a toothy, pointy-eared elf doll called Labubu became a worldwide craze, sold in sealed blind boxes and clipped to designer handbags from Bangkok to Paris. Which Chinese toy company sells it?
questions.explanation: The Beijing-based company turned a character drawn by Hong Kong artist Kasing Lung for his The Monsters series into a mystery-box phenomenon, with queues outside its stores and resale prices many times the shelf price.

questions.question: Dancers in Harlem's drag ballrooms competed by snapping into frozen poses copied from the models in one famous fashion magazine, and the dance took that magazine's name. Which magazine?
questions.explanation: Voguing was mimicking Vogue's cover poses long before Madonna's 1990 song made it a worldwide craze, and she borrowed it from the ballroom scene.

questions.question: Jaký dvouslovný nápis se skví nad jevištěm Národního divadla v Praze?

questions.question: Když na ulici potkáte kominíka, čeho se podle staré pověry máte rychle chytit, aby vám přinesl štěstí?
questions.explanation: Kdo potká kominíka, má se chytit za vlastní knoflík, a štěstí ho prý nemine. Kominík byl symbolem štěstí proto, že čistý komín chránil dům před požárem.

questions.question: Zasněžený zámek, kam Popelka ve Třech oříšcích pro Popelku přijíždí na ples, ve skutečnosti nestojí v Česku. Ve které zemi ho najdeme?
questions.explanation: Je to zámek Moritzburg u Drážďan. Každou zimu se tam koná výstava věnovaná právě Popelce.
